title: Sourdough starter
messages: ok so my sister gave me a jar of sourdough starter and i have no idea what im doing. i named him gerald. do i just feed him flour??

Congratulations on Gerald. Yes, flour and water. Discard most of the starter first, then feed him equal weights of flour and water, about 50 g of each for a small jar. Keep him at room temperature and feed him once a day for now.
ha ok. i keep him on the kitchen windowsill, is that too cold? the flat is freezing, boiler is ancient
A cold kitchen only slows him down. 20 to 24 C is ideal. Try the oven with just the light on, or the top of the fridge. You will see more bubbles in a warmer spot.
oven with the light on, genius. i'll feed him every morning at 7 before work
Seven in the morning works. Put a rubber band on the jar at the level of the starter so you can see how far he rises. When he doubles within 4 to 6 hours of a feed, he is ready to bake with.
perfect. first loaf this weekend if he behaves

title: Duplicate rows on the shipment list
messages: tracking list endpoint returns dupes when 2 shipments have the same updated_at. offset pagination i guess. can you look at api/routes/shipments.py

Found it. The list query orders by updated_at only, so rows with identical timestamps can swap places between pages. Ordering by (updated_at, id) makes the order stable. I can also move the endpoint to cursor pagination, which avoids the problem entirely. Which do you want?

cursor for the public api, definately. actually no wait, the admin endpoint is internal and only ever has a few hundred rows, offset is fine there. so cursor for public, offset + stable ordering for admin

Done. The public list now uses an opaque cursor over (updated_at, id). The admin list keeps offset pagination with the (updated_at, id) ordering. Tests pass, and I added one for two rows with the same timestamp.
nice. btw while youre in there, we're splitting atlas into three services next month: ingest, notifier and api. im the one pushing for it, i think small services are the right way to go for this team
Understood. If you do split it, the shared database schema will be the first thing to decouple. Want me to sketch the boundaries between ingest, notifier and api?
not today. i'll bring it up in planning. lunch
Enjoy lunch. The pagination change is committed on a branch and ready for a pull request.
ty, ill open the pr after. the tests are slow on this laptop so dont wait for me

title: Rust course, lesson 1
messages: just did lesson 1 of the rust for backend engineers course!! ownership already feels weird but i love it

Ownership is the big idea. Each value has one owner, and when the owner goes out of scope the value is dropped. A good exercise is to write small functions that take a String and see what the compiler tells you when you use it afterwards.
the compiler yelling at me is weirdly nice. theres another person on the course, alex moreau, we're pairing on the exercises on thursdays
Pairing is a good fit for Rust, because one of you can read the compiler's messages aloud while the other thinks about the design.
yeah. my plan is python for scripts, rust for services. im not rewriting my scripts in rust, thats silly. but anything that runs all day, rust
That split is common. Python where you want to write quickly and throw the code away, Rust where you want predictable behaviour and a small footprint over months of uptime.
exactly. ok going to do the exercises

title: Starting hearth
messages: starting a home automation thing. calling it hearth. pi 4 in the cupboard by the boiler, mosquitto for mqtt, a few temp sensors on esp32s
Good starting point. Sensors publish to topics like hearth/<room>/temp, and a collector subscribes and stores the readings. Where do you want the readings stored?
sqlite. one file, no server to babysit. its a pi, keep it small
SQLite is fine at this volume: six sensors at one reading a minute is a few thousand rows a day. I will create a readings table with (sensor, ts, value) and an index on (sensor, ts).
yes. collector in python for now, a quick script. the long running bridge between mqtt and the heating relay will be rust later, once ive got further in the course
Sounds good. I will scaffold collector.py now and leave a bridge/ directory for the Rust crate.
also the heating schedule: weekdays 6:30 to 8 in the morning and 6 to 10 in the evening
ok good. i need sleep, ill wire the relay on the weekend

title: A plan for a 10k
messages: can you make me a plan to run a 10k? i want to do a 10k in bristol on 15 march. i can currently do about 5k without dying
Yes. Ten weeks is workable from 5k. Three runs a week: two easy runs of 30 to 40 minutes and one long run that starts at 6 km and grows by about 1 km a week, with an easier week every fourth week.
i live in clifton so i mostly run on the downs. is that ok for the long run
The Downs are good for it. Keep the long run on the flatter loops at first and leave hill work until the fourth week or later.
ok. mon wed sat. goal is just to finish, not a time
A finish goal is a good one for a first 10k. Week 1 is three runs of about 20 minutes easy, with a minute of walking if you need it.
Good luck on Monday. Keep the first week easy enough that you could talk while running.
will try. i never can talk and run, ill just wheeze

title: Trekking in the Atlas Mountains
messages: planning a trek in the atlas mountains in morocco with my friend jo. toubkal, late april. where do i even start

Toubkal is the highest peak in North Africa and a realistic multi-day trek. The usual shape is flights to Marrakech, a transfer to Imlil, a few days with a guide, and guesthouses on the way. How many days, and what budget?
about 5 days. budget is 700 quid each all in, max. jo is flexible
700 pounds each for 5 days is feasible if you use local guesthouses and share the guide's cost. Flights are usually the biggest single item, so look at those first.
honestly i dont plan much, i just book things last minute and wing it. i travel spontaneously, always have. so no need for a rigid itinerary
That works for most of it. In April the guesthouse beds in Imlil can fill up, so book at least the first and last nights.
fair. if i had more money id do the 8 day guided grande traversee thing with a proper mule team lol. but 700 is 700
A budget trek of 5 days can be a very good trip. The longer guided routes are a different kind of cost, and you can always do one later.
ok ill look at flights tomorrow
Compare a few dates before you book, since flights to Marrakech can differ a lot between weekdays.
ok. jo prefers mornings so ill look at those first

title: First loaf
messages: gerald doubled in 4 hours!! baking today
That is a strong starter. For a first loaf, try 500 g bread flour, 350 g water, 100 g active starter and 10 g salt. Mix, rest, and fold the dough every 30 minutes for the first two hours.
if this works im quitting engineering to open a bakery in a cabin. gerald will be the face of the brand
Gerald's brand is secure. Meanwhile, keep the dough covered while it rests so the surface does not dry out.
ok dough resting. will report back
